name: Lightbox
summary: A full-screen image viewer that opens from thumbnails and steps through them.
description:
Use a lightbox for galleries of work, products or events, where people want to see each picture large without leaving the page.

Thumbnails are plain links to the full image with data-v-lightbox naming the viewer, so without JS they open the image itself. With JS a click opens the <dialog class="v-lightbox"> on that picture; previous and next step through every link that names the same viewer, in page order. The viewer is always dark, whatever the theme.

classes.name: v-lightbox
classes.description: The <dialog>: full screen, dark, laid out as count and close on top, the image between previous and next (under it on phones).

classes.name: v-lightbox-figure
classes.description: The <figure> holding the image and caption.

classes.name: v-lightbox-img
classes.description: The large image. Its src and alt are set from the link and its thumbnail.

classes.name: v-lightbox-caption
classes.description: The caption, from the link's data-caption. Hidden while empty.

classes.name: v-lightbox-count
classes.description: "2 of 6", in a polite live region. data-template changes the words; {n} and {total} are filled in.

classes.name: v-lightbox-prev
classes.description: The previous button. The arrow flips in right-to-left.

classes.name: v-lightbox-close
classes.description: The close control: a <form method="dialog"> with a button inside.

states.description: On a thumbnail link: the caption shown under the large image.
Set by the JS when the viewer has one picture: previous, next and the count are hidden.

hooks.name: data-v-lightbox
hooks.description: Opens the viewer on this picture instead of following the link (a modified click still opens the image in a new tab).

hooks.name: data-v-dismissable
hooks.description: A click on the dark area outside the picture closes it.

keyboard.action: On a thumbnail, opens the viewer.
Next and previous picture (swapped in right-to-left). Both wrap.
Closes the viewer and returns focus to the thumbnail.

a11y: The large image takes its alt text from the thumbnail, so write real alt text on the thumbnails.
The count is a polite live region, so stepping through announces "3 of 6" without moving focus.
Previous and next are real buttons with labels; a swipe on touch does the same, it is never the only way.
Ctrl, Cmd or Shift with a click still open the image in a new tab or window, as the link would.

examples.description: Select a picture, then use the arrows or the arrow keys.
